label: D1 after an unrewarded visit to S1, late in the episode (trial >= ~75)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2), essentially only when the reward input is 0 (previous trial unrewarded; 99.9% of mass), and only late in the episode: nothing before trial ~60, ramping up from ~70 and strongest at trials 80-99 (an episode-time / clock component). Among those steps it is specific to the previous trial having reached S1 (prev_state == 1): precision rises from 0.41 to 0.90 when this is added. Dev F1 0.84, mass recall 0.85. Most missed mass is on the first trial of the window (rel -3), where prev_state is unknown inside the window; adding those back gives mass recall 0.996 at F1 0.84. Many top examples are an a2 chooser seeing S1 via a rare transition and getting no reward, but the predicate does not need action or transition. Steps where the previous trial was rewarded, or where it was unrewarded at S2, are mostly silent. Activation is high at low model value (value < 5.2 holds 80% of mass). All variables used are observed at D1.

issues: Every factual claim held when I scored it on dev. The feature fires only at D1 (GO and D2 have 0 active steps). 99.9% of the mass has in_rew == 0. There is no activity before trial 60: 78 steps in trials 60-69, then rising. prev_state == 2 within the base condition gives precision 0. The base condition alone scores P 0.407, mass recall 0.996. Adding the rel -3 unknown case (isin(prev_state,[1,-1])) gives F1 0.84, mass recall 0.996. Value < 5.22 holds 80% of the mass. Test scores reproduce: P 0.884, R 0.787, F1 0.833, MR 0.842.

Missed activations on dev and test are mostly at rel -3, where prev_state is unknown inside the window. Outside rel -3, steps the predicate excludes hold only 0.3% of the mass. No systematic miss class.

Systematic but mild false-positive class: unrewarded common a1->S1. That path (prev_action == 1) has precision 0.771 and only 0.142 of the mass, against precision 0.987 and 0.705 of the mass for rare a2->S1 (prev_action == 2). Nearly all of the ~1357 dev false positives are a1-path steps at trials 75-84. On the a1 path the feature switches on later (precision 0.97 at ep_trial >= 85) and fires about 3x weaker. The explanation's line 'the predicate does not need action or transition' is true for the binary predicate. It undersells how much stronger the feature is after rare a2->S1.
A path-dependent onset (a1 >= 80, a2 >= 75) raises test precision to 0.94 but test F1 only to 0.836, against 0.833. That is not a meaningfully better predicate.
uses_future = false is correct: every variable in the predicate is observable at D1.
